page: Microsoft Azure D64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dalsv7 family. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the server allocates dedicated CPU resources with 2.0 threads per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it includes no local GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10% tier. Multi-core stress-ng performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the top 25% tier. Passmark CPU testing places the processor in the top 10% tier, supported by strong memory bandwidth results for both cached and uncached operations. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations and small-to-medium LLM inference text generation, alongside strong static web serving throughput.

Given its low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and lack of local storage, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The high clock speed of 4.5 GHz and strong single-core performance make it highly suitable for compute-intensive tasks, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
